notes: Step 1 parts were correct: no parts added or dropped.
Circuit follows the schematic: board pin 2 -> 220 ohm resistor -> LED anode; LED cathode -> GND.

In the image the resistor spans breadboard columns 3 and 6 and the LED legs sit in columns 6 and 8. The bent leg shares column 6 with the resistor, so it is the anode. The other leg in column 8 is the cathode and takes the black wire to GND.

The image labels the upper breadboard half as rows f-j, but the catalogue names the upper half bank 't' with rows a-e. I used the catalogue names. Every column strip is the same either way, so the connectivity matches the image.
The exact row letter in each column is a guess, because the strip is what matters electrically. The resistor, LED and wires each use a different hole in their column.
The catalogue card for the MKR WiFi 1010 has a single GND port, so the black wire goes to GND and the green wire to D2.
The Micro USB cable is joined to the board's USB port only. It powers and programs the board and is not part of the LED circuit. The catalogue lists no ports for the cable, so its port is null.
